sections.title: Growth and flowers
sections.text: Charlock, or wild mustard, is an annual brassica about 20–100 cm tall, with lobed lower leaves and yellow, four-petalled flowers about 1 cm across. Its narrow pods are about 2.5–4 cm long, ending in a beak about 0.8–1.2 cm long. Height varies with growing conditions.

sections.title: Food and caution
sections.text: A university extension guide reports edible uses for several parts, including young greens and seeds. As with other mustards, seed and greens have a pungent mustard flavour; mustard allergy is possible. Do not confuse it with white mustard (S. alba), whose fruit has a conspicuously flattened beak.
